picks.text: Dubai is my lean after its 107–91 win over Bayern lifted it to five wins in seven games. Paris enters after losing to Valencia and sits at one win in seven. The contrast is noticeable, although both clubs' incomplete injury reports make this a cautious call rather than a priced recommendation.

I lean Panathinaikos at home: it improved to six wins from seven by beating Baskonia 85–79, while Milan lost 89–81 to Barcelona last round. One strong start does not guarantee another, and the latest squad reports should be checked before treating the matchup as settled.

Barcelona gets the narrow nod after beating Milan for its fourth win, while Bayern comes off a 107–91 defeat to Dubai. Barcelona reports Dario Brizuela available and Yoan Makoundou out; Bayern had not yet submitted its report. Away-court uncertainty keeps the call modest.

Real Madrid is the tentative choice after scoring 113 against Maccabi in its latest EuroLeague win. The official standings list Madrid at 4–3 and Baskonia at 1–6. Seven games are a small sample and the visit to Vitoria still calls for a fresh lineup check.

Fenerbahce narrowly gets my vote after holding Olympiacos to 61 points and improving to 6–1. Valencia is also 5–2 after beating Paris 104–93, so this is far from a routine away game. Valencia lists Nate Reuvers out; other late changes remain possible.

Jodar is the lean in Basel after beating Tabilo 6–2, 6–1 in Cincinnati, where the ATP recorded a 2–1 head-to-head lead. That previous result provides a useful reference, not a guarantee: the surface, day-to-day form and any late fitness news can alter the picture.

Hurkacz gets a slight edge on the evidence of his recent Shanghai run, where he beat Djokovic before losing to eventual champion Davidovich Fokina. Bergs is a capable opponent and the court schedule can change, so I would not turn a modest preference into a confident price.

Lehecka is the tentative pick against Wawrinka, with the ATP listing him as the eighth seed and reporting a Tokyo final earlier this month. Wawrinka has a home farewell and this is their first meeting, so there is little direct matchup evidence and the start is sequential.

Djokovic gets the lean after winning their only previous meeting at Wimbledon and holding a 12–2 Basel record, according to the ATP. Humbert has won four tour titles indoors, though, making this an awkward opening match. Wednesday's exact starting time was not established.

Van de Zandschulp is the narrow preference after the ATP results list his 6–4, 6–4 win over Michelsen in Shanghai on 10 October. One recent meeting cannot settle a rematch, and their Basel match follows others on court one, so the actual start is not fixed here.

Glasgow is my home lean after an unbeaten opening four rounds, with three wins and a draw. The Lions have two wins and two losses and just lost 31–10 at Edinburgh. Four matches are not a complete form guide, while team selection and the draw remain important uncertainties.

The Stormers are the tentative choice: the URC table shows three wins from four and their latest result was a 52–40 win over Scarlets. Ulster has drawn twice and lost twice, but scoring 26 at the Bulls shows why a result cannot be assumed from the standings alone.

I lean to the Sharks on early-season results: three wins from four and a 36–21 victory at Cardiff, compared with Munster's one win and one draw. This is still an away fixture, team selections are unconfirmed and a rugby draw is a genuine separate outcome.

Leinster is the smallest of leans in a meeting of sides with identical two-win, two-loss records. The visitors beat Munster 24–18 in the previous round, while Connacht scored 48 against Zebre. That close comparison and unknown selections argue against a strong confidence label.

Magdeburg gets the selection after winning all five group games and beating Kriens-Luzern 39–29 in their first meeting. Both clubs lead their domestic leagues, and neither has a qualification place left to decide here. Rotation and the possibility of a draw make the call less certain than the record alone suggests.

Veszprem is the lean after five straight group wins, including a 36–28 home victory over Porto. Porto drew with Partizan in the last round and is already out, but both teams lead their domestic leagues. Qualification is settled, so late rotation could change the balance.

Kielce gets the nod after a 36–29 win at Kolstad in the reverse fixture. The EHF lists seven Kielce wins in seven previous meetings and no group points for Kolstad, yet both teams' qualification positions are fixed. That creates lineup uncertainty before this final group game.

Berlin is my pick after a 44–33 away win in the reverse fixture. Partizan had not won a group game before the last round, although its draw with Porto shows it can compete. Berlin has already advanced, so check the actual team before making too much of the earlier margin.

Barcelona is the selection after winning all five group matches and defeating Aarhus 39–28 in their first meeting. Aarhus still has a qualification incentive and plays at home, whereas Barcelona is already through. Those different circumstances are reasons to check lineups and avoid assuming a repeat score.

Bergamo gets a cautious preference away to Marignano. The league's table after four matches showed Bergamo with three wins, while the official preview notes the visitors' strong opening and the hosts' need for points. Early standings are thin evidence, and team availability has not been established.

Conegliano is the home lean, but Vallefoglia deserves respect: both had won all four league matches when the league published its preview. Conegliano had taken all 12 sets, while Vallefoglia needed one tiebreak. A short early-season sample and unconfirmed lineups limit the strength of this selection.

Hobart is the tentative choice for its opener after winning the previous WBBL title. Cricket Australia reports that the Hurricanes launch their defence against Melbourne Stars at Junction Oval. Last season's title is useful context, not evidence of the final squads, weather or a reliable current price.

Milwaukee is the cautious lean after moving 3–0 ahead in the World Series with a 10–1 Game 3 win. That result does not determine Game 4: MLB had Milwaukee's starter to be announced and listed Griffin Jax for Tampa Bay, so pitching news is an important unresolved factor.

Clark is my outright preference after three PGA Tour wins in 2026, including the U.S. Open, and a top-25 finish on his previous visit to Vidanta Vallarta. An outright field is inherently difficult to beat; an opening quote from yesterday is historical, not evidence of today's available price.

picks.text: Woad is the tentative outright choice. The LPGA lists her in the Maybank field and records a win at the 2026 Kroger Queen City Championship. A large field leaves plenty of ways for this pick to miss, and neither a current price nor first-round tee time is established here.

Cink is the cautious outright preference based on five PGA Tour Champions wins entering the playoffs and his position atop the Schwab Cup standings at that point. The field remains deep, and this is not a forecast that he is more likely than everyone else combined to win.

Dobey is a speculative tournament-winner lean in a 128-player field. The PDC lists him among the confirmed entries and reports two Players Championship titles this season in its qualification update. A long knockout route makes any individual winner uncertain, and no current bookmaker quote is available here.

I lean Columbus in a close game, though neither side has a clean recent trend. Fantilli's overtime power-play goal beat Vegas 2–1 after Columbus had lost four of its previous five. Philadelphia reported Ristolainen out and York a possible return, but starting goalies and final lineups could change the balance.

Carolina gets a narrow home-ice lean after a 4–0 win at St. Louis brought its record to 9–2–2. Aho and Jarvis each had two points in that game, and Hall could return from injury. Boston is a serious opponent, however; confirm the goalies and Hall's status before treating this as more than a lean.

Florida is my tentative road pick after its 3–2 win in Chicago ended a two-game skid. The Panthers reported Tkachuk had 16 points in 12 games; Winnipeg had lost five straight, scoring more than twice only once in that spell. That small sample and unconfirmed goalies keep confidence modest.

Dallas gets the slightest home lean: it came back to beat the Islanders 6–3 after earlier overtime wins over Boston and Winnipeg. The Stars' own report also listed Duchene out and Lindell and Bäck missing weeks. New Jersey and the current starting goalies need closer review, so this is not a strong call.

Nashville is the tentative home side after a 6–2 win over Colorado in which it scored four power-play goals. The Islanders' preview noted Nashville had lost five of six before that win, while New York's five-game point streak also just ended. Confirm starting goalies; neither short run guarantees the next result.

Antonelli is my podium lean in Mexico. He took his ninth Grand Prix win of the season in Austin, starting from pole and finishing 13.078 seconds ahead of Leclerc. Track-specific practice and qualifying remain unknown, and a mechanical problem or incident can erase recent form; no current podium quote was established.

Oyonnax gets the home lean, but Soyaux-Angoulême is not an easy opponent. The official Pro D2 table had Oyonnax first with seven wins from eight, while the visitors were fourth. Oyonnax lost its most recent match at Montauban, so the edge is not automatic; team sheets and draw settlement need checking.

India is the lean after two successful four-wicket chases in Christchurch, including a tight finish in the second T20. New Zealand still has home conditions and Glenn Phillips made 70 last time. India batter Ishan Kishan was ruled out of this game, while New Zealand is rotating its quicks; wait for the toss and final XIs.

Pakistan gets the home lean after three wins from three in the ODI tri-series. PCB reports a 37-run victory over Sri Lanka in their first meeting, with Salman Ali Agha making 107. Sri Lanka also chased successfully against England, so the match remains competitive; Pakistan has already qualified and its XI needs a pre-toss check.

Afghanistan is the lean after beating Zimbabwe in the recent ODI tri-series final, with Ibrahim Zadran unbeaten on 70 and Rashid Khan taking three wickets. The format now changes to T20, so the ODI result is context rather than a direct forecast; Zimbabwe's Sikandar Raza made 68 in that final and can change a short game.

Phoebe Litchfield is a tentative choice to top-score for Sydney Thunder. Cricket Australia reports she led the team with 271 runs at a strike rate of 150 last season, but Georgia Voll and Heather Knight add competition. Georgia Wareham dismissed her for 12 in their previous meeting; check the starting XI and batting order.
